evidence: Receiving delayed assay at 48 h: P = 3.066 g/L, matching source batches (3.057, 3.017, 2.979 g/L)
Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 10.95 mg/L vs sources 10.88/10.81/11.47 mg/L at same time
All batches (source and receiving) show DO2 minima ~7.4 mg/L near 72-75 h, far above the 2.0 mg/L constraint
Source batches reach peak P ~8 g/L at 72-84 h while DO stays non-limiting; receiving is mid-production at 52 h
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation closely reproduces the source process trajectory: P(48h)=3.07 g/L matches the sources' 2.98-3.06 g/L, and DO at 52 h (10.9 mg/L) is near-identical to all three source batches. DO has never approached the 2.0 mg/L minimum in any observed run (historical trough ~7.4 mg/L at 72-75 h, which is non-limiting for growth and product formation). Product is still rising mid-run; reducing feed would slow production, extra air is unnecessary given large DO headroom, and a stop yields zero counted production. This is a normal case requiring no intervention.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters may differ from sources, so future DO could theoretically dip lower than any source run; however, with the observed minimum being ~3.7x the constraint margin and consistent behavior across four trajectories, oxygen violation risk under KEEP is very low. Downstream product decline (as seen after ~84 h in sources) is a known feature of the process, not something the offered interventions (feed/air) clearly improve, and harvest timing is outside the decision scope.
